feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader with clear progression, relevant scope, and solid technical breadth. It reads professionally and is mostly polished, but it would be stronger with tighter structure, more quantified outcomes, and a few wording/style fixes to improve consistency and impact.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within one organization, showing increasing responsibility from coordinator to director to consultant.  
- Strong relevance for digital strategy roles: web, CMS, analytics, governance, email, social, and multimedia are all well covered.  
- Good credibility through concrete scale indicators such as “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and named tools/platforms.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more outcome-focused metrics beyond scope/activity: e.g., traffic growth, engagement lifts, email performance, efficiency gains, cost savings, or adoption improvements.  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; the CV repeats similar themes and could be streamlined for sharper structure.  
- Fix minor writing/style issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12 years of experience”; maintain consistent serial comma usage (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”); “A2/Learning” is stylistically awkward—use “French (A2, currently learning)” instead.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and scope, but it reads slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and anchoring it more directly to public-sector/advocacy digital leadership would increase impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience.”
- Lead with your niche: digital strategy and communications leadership for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Replace broad phrases like “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs” with a tighter, higher-value framing around cross-channel strategy, platform modernization, and operational systems.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience building and leading cross-channel programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in web and CMS modernization, editorial and operational workflow design, and integrated communications across web, email, social, and multimedia. Strong track record in advocacy messaging, stakeholder alignment, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows and systems” are repeated in Core Competencies/Topline Skills.
- “Stakeholder coordination” also overlaps with Soft Skills and experience bullets.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT sections. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing leadership-level capabilities will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, higher-impact phrasing: “Digital transformation strategy,” “Cross-channel communications leadership,” “CMS and web operations,” “Editorial systems and governance.”
- Replace vague or repetitive items like “Workflow & systems architecture” with more specific language such as “Content operations and workflow design” or “Digital governance and process design.”
- Standardize style: change “Multi-channel communication” to “Multichannel communications” for consistency and polish.
- Consider a tighter version: Digital transformation strategy • Multichannel communications leadership • CMS and web operations • Editorial systems and governance • Analytics and performance reporting • Content operations and process design • Cross-functional stakeholder leadership • Advocacy and policy communications • Multimedia and live event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Strong overlap with the header summary and all four Topline Skills categories.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” also repeats Soft Skills almost verbatim.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo role below and Recent Projects. Tighten it around consultant-level outcomes, transformation work, and 2–3 signature contributions.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + value: “Advise NACo on enterprise web strategy, digital governance, and campaign platform development for member-facing communications.”
- Replace generic verbs with outcome-oriented phrasing: “Redesigned workflows and analytics for cross-team communications operations” instead of “Build and refine digital systems…”
- Consolidate technical delivery: combine CMS/front-end/troubleshooting into one bullet focused on impact to major public-facing properties.
- Add measurable signals where possible: number of sites/pages supported, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, time saved, search/discovery improvements, stakeholder groups served.

Suggested edit example:
- Advise NACo on enterprise web strategy, digital governance, and campaign platform development for member-facing communications.
- Built Drupal microsites, modular storytelling components, and downloadable toolkits to support advocacy and member campaigns.
- Improved cross-team content workflows, analytics, and publishing operations across web, email, social, and multimedia.
- Led an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content workflows, and user discovery experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search” and microsite work also appear in Recent Projects; avoid repeating the same detail in both places.
- Governance/analytics/workflows strongly overlap with the 2022–2024 NACo role; emphasize consultant scope and new initiatives.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground the biggest outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance and budget management.”
- Prioritize the strongest achievements in 4–5 bullets: website migration, analytics stack, video studio, governance/operations, and channel reach only if you can add stronger performance metrics.
- Rewrite for action + outcome, e.g.: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable impact where possible: email growth/open rates, social engagement, reporting efficiency, production cost savings, faster publishing, reduced vendor reliance, or improved stakeholder adoption.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video/programming language overlaps with older NACo roles and footer projects; emphasize building the in-house studio and organizational capacity instead.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps with the more senior NACo roles and reads too generally. Tighten it around executional leadership, channel ownership, and any measurable growth or process improvements achieved before promotion.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + progression: “Managed day-to-day digital communications across NACo’s web, email, social, and video channels, scaling editorial operations and advocacy messaging during a period of organizational growth.”
- Combine bullets and sharpen verbs: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders; coordinated publishing calendars and cross-team content inputs.”
- Make the video bullet outcome-focused: “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel across web, email, and social.”
- Replace vague workflow language with specifics if available: note turnaround time, publishing volume, stakeholder groups supported, or process improvements that increased consistency.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Strengthened editorial planning” and “improved publishing workflows” overlap with the Director role’s governance/planning bullets.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role; distinguish this item by emphasizing ownership and scale.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should be tightened to emphasize senior-level leadership scope and the most distinctive, recent strengths.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy & stakeholder messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “audience-focused content planning” for “content operations” or “web modernization,” which better reflects recent leadership-level work.
- Keep wording parallel: use either all noun phrases or all “X & Y” constructions for cleaner scanability.
- If space allows elsewhere, reserve broader terms here and let work experience carry specifics like Drupal, AI search, analytics, and multimedia.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” repeat the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” overlaps with Core Competencies’ “Multi-channel communications operations.”

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it’s too tool-heavy and overlaps with the Technical + IT section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value capabilities tied to recent Drupal modernization and AI/search work, not a full software inventory.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from platform list to capability-led phrasing: “Drupal and enterprise CMS delivery” is stronger than listing every CMS equally.
- Cut lower-priority or older-feeling items here (e.g., jQuery, WordPress if not central to recent roles) and keep the most relevant to current work.
- Group related items for concision and seniority: “Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript), API integrations, workflow automation.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end web implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • SharePoint and Power Pages • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates the “Technical + IT” section; keep Topline Skills broader and reserve full tool lists for Technical + IT.
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” also echo Core Competencies—avoid repeating exact phrasing if possible.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization

- Power BI

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize strategic analytics capability, not repeat software names alone.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing: “Analytics strategy, KPI design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis.”
- Keep only the most differentiating tools and group them: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity.”
- Tighten wording and show business use: “Dashboarding and insight generation for leadership decision-making” instead of just “Leadership reporting.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy and KPI design • Executive dashboards and leadership reporting • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • SEO, UX and performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Core Competencies: Analytics and reporting infrastructure” and “Technical + IT: Data, Analytics & Optimization.”
- Avoid adding A/B testing here unless you also reflect it in recent experience with evidence.

Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize operational leadership and recent in-house studio/event delivery impact rather than basic production tasks.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section. Since recent experience is heavily Drupal-centered, lead with that and consider trimming lower-signal tools.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** is fine, but consider emphasizing depth: **Drupal (enterprise migration, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add a light qualifier instead of just names: **Enterprise CMS: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**
- Consider dropping **GitHub Pages** unless it supports a notable project; it feels less aligned with the senior enterprise/public-sector positioning.
- If this section should stay tool-only, keep it very concise and let work experience carry outcomes.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**, which already lists Drupal, WordPress, and SharePoint.
- “CMS modernization” in Topline Skills already conveys platform breadth; avoid repeating the same list in two places without added specificity.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools not already covered elsewhere and use cleaner, current phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Technical Implementation: HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless required by the role; “HTML/CSS” is cleaner and more current.
- Group related items for readability: Front-end (HTML/CSS, JavaScript/jQuery) • Integrations/Tagging (API integrations, GTM) • Deployment/Edge (Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions)
- If space allows elsewhere, connect 1–2 tools to outcomes in recent roles instead of listing more tools here (e.g., GTM for analytics setup, GitHub Actions for deployment automation).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact phrasing in both places.
- “Workflow automation” in Topline Skills may partially overlap with GitHub Actions.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow leadership. Since workflow automation is already highlighted elsewhere, this item should be tighter and more systems-oriented.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe by function, not just brand names: “Workflow automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/issue management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Team collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams”
- Put the strongest, most relevant tools first: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana.
- If true, add scope in a parenthetical: “used to support cross-team editorial planning, approvals, intake, and communications operations.”
- Consider dropping one or two lower-value/general tools (e.g., Slack, Teams, Basecamp) if space is tight; they are widely assumed and less differentiating.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp overlap as project tools; listing all four may feel padded unless each was materially used.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as generic software inventory rather than evidence of email/engagement capability. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this item should stay concise and tool-focused.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten platform names for readability and consistency: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add one capability cue instead of more tools: **campaign automation, newsletter operations, audience segmentation**
- Keep this as a short stack line, not a sentence, to preserve space and avoid repeating accomplishments already covered in work experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding outcomes like newsletter reach or channel leadership here; those are already covered in the 2022–2024 and 2018–2022 NACo roles.
- “Multi-channel communications operations” already appears in Core Competencies, so don’t broaden this item beyond email/engagement platforms.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful scope, but the item is still generic and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize “firsts,” team-building, and channel ownership without repeating website/video points covered above.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground advancement and team-building: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Tighten the second sentence around concrete outputs: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, expanding the organization’s in-house publishing capacity.”
- Replace “high-impact” with measurable outcomes if available: number of livestreams, frequency of video series, audience growth, or production volume.
- Clarify supervision scope: “provided day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate” → “mentored a digital media associate on daily production and publishing workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this as launching or early producing rather than expanding.
- “Website refresh” may feel repetitive with the later Drupal redesign; keep this framed as an earlier refresh, not a major modernization.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Emphasize cross-functional coordination and the launch outcome, while keeping it concise.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; launched the organization’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- Tighten vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” to something more active: “produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications.”
- If possible, add scope or output: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, audiences reached, or types of stakeholders/program teams served.
- Consider a two-part structure: policy/program support first, then digital/media contribution, to show range without overexplaining.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia” overlaps with later Digital Media Manager / Producer and Associate Communications Director roles; avoid repeating broad multimedia language.
- Since later roles already establish video leadership, keep this item focused on podcast launch and innovation/project coordination.
